answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small refundable deposit before it may trade, like a garden that only grows for those who tend it. The deposit is slashed on proven fraud, so creating thousands of fake agents costs real money while honest agents earn it back. A reputation delta then separates newcomers from proven actors: new identities start with a low trust score and gain weight only through verified, useful work over time, the way a sonnet earns its form line by line. Fake identities stay cheap to spot and expensive to scale.
